main.description: A puzzle published by a host, presented to solvers via body and checked against answers.

body.description: The puzzle itself, as presented to solvers -- including anything a solver needs to see before answering (prompts, clue text, instructions). Not encrypted.

meta.description: Client-side info relevant only when actually viewing the puzzle -- not descriptive metadata like title or author, which stay their own top-level protocol fields. Not encrypted; nothing in here is secret.

answers.description: Encrypted. Decrypts to { answers: [{ id: string, name: string, canonical: string, alternates: string[] }], hints: [{ match: string, message: string }] }. Holds only answer-verification data -- anything visible to a solver before answering (prompts, clue text) belongs in body, not here. hints are not tied to a specific answer: each is an arbitrary near-miss string that surfaces a message without counting as solved. Opaque to the lexicon by design, so its internal shape can change freely without a protocol-level compatibility concern.

publishAt.description: When the puzzle becomes visible to solvers. Optional -- if absent, the puzzle is visible as soon as it's indexed. Distinct from createdAt: a puzzle can be authored well ahead of its scheduled release.

format.description: How clients should interpret body -- e.g. which markdown flavor is in use. No fixed set of values yet.
